purpose: Compact, low-power local-AI mini PCs that add useful deployment or value characteristics without treating platform TOPS as LLM token-generation performance.

memory_bandwidth.note: Derived from AMD's dual-channel DDR5-5600 platform capability; PistonV has not published a measured system-memory bandwidth result.

software: AMD Ryzen AI software for XDNA 2 workloads
hardware.model_size_practicality: The base 16GB configuration is mainly suitable for small quantized models. A 64GB configuration can hold many 7B-32B GGUF models in system RAM and selected larger quantized models, but DDR5 bandwidth and shared CPU/GPU memory make capacity much less important than throughput for large-model decode.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: CPU and Vulkan/llama.cpp paths can use common GGUF quantizations. XDNA 2 acceleration depends on supported Ryzen AI/ONNX models and must not be assumed to accelerate arbitrary GGUF, GPTQ or AWQ models.
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Interesting low-cost expandable mini PC for small-to-medium local LLMs, RAG, agent orchestration and experimentation. OCuLink can add a discrete GPU later without relying on USB4 bandwidth.

performance_per_watt.note: AMD publishes a 15-54W processor cTDP range, but no defensible Piston V whole-system tokens-per-watt measurement is available.

hardware.off_grid_suitability: Potentially good for a compact x86 node because the processor can operate in a 15-54W envelope, but whole-system idle/load power and DC-input details are not yet published.

pricing.note: Current early-bird campaign tier reported at US$589 for the base 16GB/500GB configuration; crowdfunding carries delivery and final-spec risk. The sold-out super-early-bird tier was US$559, standard campaign tier US$679, and stated post-campaign retail target US$799.

hardware.model_size_practicality: 16GB soldered memory makes small quantized models the practical target. Roughly 1B-7B GGUF-class models can fit depending on quantization and context, but this is an entry-level AI/edge system rather than a high-throughput LLM node.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: CPU inference can use common GGUF quantizations. Intel's NPU supports OpenVINO/ONNX-oriented INT8 workflows; the 15-TOPS NPU figure does not imply generic llama.cpp/GGUF acceleration.
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Best suited to lightweight local assistants, embeddings, OCR, speech, small RAG pipelines and always-on edge tasks. The single Xe core and 16GB fixed RAM substantially limit larger-model inference.

performance_per_watt.note: Intel specifies 15W base and 35W maximum turbo processor power. MINIX has not published a normalized whole-system LLM tokens-per-watt result.

hardware.off_grid_suitability: Potentially good for lightweight always-on AI because of the 10-35W processor envelope, but complete-system idle/load power and input-voltage details should be measured before deployment planning.

pricing.note: Authorized European channel lists the 16GB/512GB Windows 11 Pro configuration at €749.99 but out of stock.
